title: Dynamic Discrete Choice and Inverse Reinforcement Learning: Inferring Preferences and Beliefs From Human Behavior
abstract: arXiv:2608.24362v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This article surveys two deeply connected literatures that approach the same fundamental problem from different disciplinary traditions: dynamic discrete choice (DDC) in structural econometrics and inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) in machine learning. Both seek to infer the preferences of decision makers from observed sequential behavior, assuming that individuals act to maximize an expected reward function within a dynamic, uncertain environment formalized as a Markov decision process (MDP).   Despite independent origins, the two fields have converged on similar mathematical formulations. We show that the (soft Q-learning) framework now prevalent in IRL is closely related to DDC models under additive extreme value preference shocks, yielding the same softmax (multinomial logit) choice probabilities and smooth Bellman equations that underpin structural estimation in economics. translated_title: 动态离散选择与逆强化学习：从人类行为中推断偏好与信念
translated_abstract: 本文综述了两个深度关联的研究领域，它们从不同的学科传统出发，探讨同一根本性问题：结构计量经济学中的动态离散选择（DDC）和机器学习中的逆强化学习（IRL）。两者都旨在从观察到的序列行为中推断决策者的偏好，假设个体在动态、不确定的环境中，以最大化预期奖励函数为目标，该环境被形式化为马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）。尽管起源独立，这两个领域在数学表述上已趋同。我们表明，当前IRL中流行的（软Q学习）框架与具有加性极值偏好冲击的DDC模型密切相关，产生相同的softmax（多项logit）选择概率和平滑贝尔曼方程，这些方程支撑了经济学中的结构估计。我们比较了各自发展的估计和计算方法。
tldr: 本文揭示了动态离散选择与逆强化学习在数学上的本质等价性，并系统比较了两者在偏好推断中的方法互补性。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals the mathematical equivalence between dynamic discrete choice and inverse reinforcement learning, systematically comparing their complementary methods for preference inference.
